text: People used to shave the edges off their coins, and then spend them anyway!
Back then, a silver coin was worth the silver inside it.
So shave a little off a hundred coins, melt the shavings, and you have free silver!
This was called clipping, and you could be put to death for it.
So in sixteen sixty-two, England began making coins by machine, with a pattern on the edge.
Now a shaved coin was easy to spot!
But old smooth coins were still everywhere. So in sixteen ninety-six, England remade all its money.
And the man hunting the cheaters was Isaac Newton!
His biggest target was a forger named William Chaloner, who even faked the edges.
Newton questioned the witnesses himself, and Chaloner was hanged.
Today's coins are not silver. But the ridges stayed, and they help blind people tell coins apart by touch!
So those ridges are a leftover from when people shaved their money!
